title: How Zach Yadegari launched Flow Alarm: subscription upsell, LTV-based CAC, and cash discipline
summary: Episode 1 of Zach's open-source journey building Flow, a physical alarm-clock dock. He covers picking a big-TAM product, pre-selling during a manufacturing delay, and fixing unit economics with a subscription attach at checkout. The key lesson: spend up to full LTV on acquisition while testing pricing and verifying data.

principles.text: Pick products with huge TAM that everyone uses daily, especially where incumbents aren't innovating.
principles.quote: The things with the biggest TAMs are really the things that everyone uses on a [music] day-to-day basis. And some of the biggest companies are just companies that aren't innovating on [music] some of the technologies people use every day.

principles.text: Pre-sell with scarcity and honest ship delays instead of waiting on slow manufacturing.
principles.quote: We put a pre-sale, but we did [music] it in a very unique way. Made it feel like there was a lot of scarcity, but we made it clear like your order is not going to ship for a while, but get it now.

principles.text: Keep media buying simple: master the fundamentals and turn off Meta's extra automations.
principles.quote: turning off all the extra [ __ ] that Metatries to turn on for you and just keeping it [music] simple stupid.

principles.text: Raise LTV with a subscription attached to the product; that's what unlocks scaling spend.
principles.quote: So, what's going to take us to the millions is increasing the LTV, which will mostly come from the subscriptions.

principles.text: When revenue recurs, spend up to full LTV on acquisition and profit on renewals, not day one.
principles.quote: A smart business person would recognize that this $41 is a recurring subscription. the smart business person would spend $41.

principles.text: Don't trust a single dashboard; trace anomalies to the root and A/B test price points.
principles.quote: We use triple whale and I realize all of this data is [ __ ] inaccurate.
